UNUSED_ACTOR on A:rival: declared as an actor, associated with no epic or use case

# STATE LITERALS ALREADY IN THE MODEL (reuse these exact ids where they fit)
- S:belt_exists -- a belt of rocks exists
- S:controls_live -- the controls answer the pilot
- S:gem_in_hold -- gem credits are in the hold
- S:gem_pickable -- a gem can be picked up
- S:gems_loose -- gems are loose in the world
- S:gems_spilled -- the hold is on the floor
- S:hull_swapped -- the ship is flying a new frame
- S:in_combat -- damage is being exchanged
- S:in_flight -- the pilot is flying and in control
- S:page_open -- the page is open and nothing has started
- S:point_banked -- the pilot is owed at least one upgrade point
- S:respawned -- the pilot is flying again after dying
- S:rock_in_range -- a rock is within reach
- S:save_current -- the stored snapshot is no more than one interval old
- S:save_gathered -- a snapshot of the run exists
- S:save_restored -- a returning pilot has their ship back
- S:save_written -- the snapshot is in storage
- S:session_recorded -- the run is over and what happened is on record
- S:shield_stripped -- a shield arc is down
- S:ship_dead -- the pilot's ship is destroyed
- S:ship_exists -- the pilot has a ship in that world
- S:ship_stronger -- the ship is measurably better than it was
- S:shot_in_flight -- a shot is travelling
- S:sim_running -- the simulation is stepping
- S:stat_raised -- at least one stat is above zero
- S:stats_maxed -- every stat is at its cap
- S:tier_offered -- a next hull is on offer
- S:under_fire -- something is shooting at the pilot
- S:weapon_ready -- the ship can fire
- S:world_built -- a world exists to fly in

# THE ANSWER MUST SATISFY
- One use case is one actor goal achieved in one sitting.
- Preconditions and postconditions are state literals with ids like S:gem_in_hold; reuse an existing id whenever the meaning matches.
- The order of the story is derived from those states, so getting them right matters more than the order you list the use cases in.
- Cite only symbols from the ground atoms above.
- status HAVE needs a citation; ABSENT is a real and useful answer.

# QUESTION (UNUSED_ACTOR)
A:rival 'Another ship' is declared as an actor and performs nothing, so nothing in the model is done on its behalf. Either name the use cases it performs -- what does this actor want, and which beats of which epic serve that? -- or say it should not be an actor at all, which is equally a finding.

# OBLIGATION
Your patch must place A:rival in the chain with a precedes edge.

# ANSWER FORMAT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

{
  "reasoning": "one or two sentences: why this is the answer",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "UC-...", "kind": "usecase|step|state|actor",
     "name": "Actor verbs an object",
     "attrs": {"story": "...", "status": "HAVE|PARTIAL|ABSENT|INFERRED",
               "ground": ["symbolName"], "acceptance": ["a falsifiable check"]}}
  ],
  "edges": [{"src": "...", "dst": "...", "kind": "includes|precedes|requires|establishes|extends|performs|groundedIn"}],
  "abstain": false,
  "abstain_reason": ""
}

Rules that are enforced, not advisory:
- Every symbol in "ground" must be one of the ground atoms listed above. A symbol that
  is not in that list is a hallucination and the patch is refused.
- status HAVE requires at least one ground symbol. If nothing in the source implements
  it, say status ABSENT -- that is a finding, not a failure.
- One use case is one actor goal. If the name needs "and", it is two use cases.
- Reuse an existing state id when the meaning matches; do not invent a synonym.
- If you genuinely cannot answer from what you were given, set abstain true and say why.
  An honest abstention is recorded as an open question; a guess is worse than a hole.
